manufacturer.schneider.description: The German brand that moved from distributing Amstrad computers to offering its own Euro and Tower ranges.
manufacturer.schneider.history: Schneider Computer Division, part of Schneider Rundfunkwerke in Türkheim, marketed the Amstrad PC1512 and PC1640. In 1987 it introduced the PC2640 as its own design; contemporary reporting distinguished that design from initial manufacture abroad. The 1988 EuroPC brought this new direction into the home, housing the computer and floppy drive in the keyboard. EuroPC II and EuroXT broadened the range, while EuroAT and Tower addressed other formats and needs. Euro486 and D486/20 appeared as separate lines in 1991. A shared brand does not establish a common OEM origin for every machine.
